response.justification: The candidate is an experienced full-stack/web software engineer with ~14 years of professional experience, but the resume shows essentially no overlap with the core requirements of a Principal Performance Architect role in AI accelerator hardware. There is no evidence of SoC/IP modeling, hardware-software co-design, GPU or SIMD/MIMD architecture work, or deep-learning training/inference optimization. The closest adjacent experience is low-latency service work in D at Sociomantic and some C/C++ at National Instruments, which is application-level rather than silicon-level performance engineering. The BS in Computer Science plus 8+ years satisfies the educational bar, but the domain expertise required for a principal-level IC in accelerator architecture is absent.
strengths: 14+ years of broad software engineering experience across web, mobile, desktop, and embedded
Demonstrated low-latency, high-throughput systems work (millions of req/s at Sociomantic)
Strong C/C++ exposure at National Instruments plus open-source leadership and public speaking
concerns: No SoC/IP modeling, RTL, or hardware architecture experience whatsoever
No deep-learning, GPU, or AI accelerator workload optimization background
Career trajectory is web/full-stack, not principal-level silicon performance architecture

key_factors.factor: Extensive general software engineering tenure and systems-level performance work
